item.title: Music Beneath the Radio Calls

turns.text: Add a tense instrumental bed to this. Keep it under the radio calls so every word is easy to hear, especially 'Rook, you with me?' Don't change the footage.

item.tests: Tests whether added music remains audibly subordinate to the original speech, with intelligibility preserved throughout the delivered video.

answer_sheet.Music mood and vocals: Tense instrumental music, with no singing.
answer_sheet.Music level relative to speech: Clearly quieter than the radio calls whenever someone speaks; every original word must remain easy to hear.
answer_sheet.Source footage, duration, and framing: Keep the entire attached 7-second cockpit clip, with unchanged visuals, timing, and framing.
answer_sheet.Speech and added text: Keep the original radio-call recording in sync. Do not replace it or add text.

must_haves: The output preserves all seven seconds of the original cockpit footage without visual changes or extra shots.
A tense instrumental music bed is audible, with no added singing.
The original radio calls remain present and synchronized, including the clearly intelligible line 'Rook, you with me?'
During every spoken line, the music is perceptibly below the voice and does not mask words with loud beats, swells, or accents.
The music is not simply muted for the entire clip; it is audible while remaining subordinate to speech.

turns.text: Add a tense instrumental bed to the attached clip. Keep it under the radio calls so every word is easy to hear, especially “Rook, you with me?” Don’t change the footage. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do this?

dialog.agent:
**Nothing has run, and no credits have been spent.**

To keep the footage unchanged and every radio call clear, the best approach is to add music as a separate audio layer—not use AI video editing, which could alter the visuals.

### Cost and cheaper options
| Option | Magic Hour cost |
|---|---:|
| Generate a tense instrumental | **1 credit per second, 15-second minimum** |
| Generate a 15-second bed, then trim or loop it | **15 credits** |
| Use an existing track you own or a suitably licensed free track | **0 generation credits** |

A shorter generation below 15 seconds won’t reduce the minimum charge. Lowering the video resolution won’t make music generation cheaper, and there’s no need to shrink your footage.

**One limitation:** the connected tools can generate music, but they don’t provide a soundtrack-mixing control to duck it beneath your existing dialogue while preserving the footage. That final mix would need a free editor such as Shotcut or DaVinci Resolve.

For the mix, I’d keep the bed restrained, lower it further during all radio calls, and dip it especially deeply around **“Rook, you with me?”**—without replacing or regenerating the original audio.

**My recommendation:** use a free licensed instrumental for the lowest cost, or start with a **15-second, 15-credit** generated bed. How long is the clip, and which option would you prefer?
dialog.user: The clip is 7 seconds. ok, go ahead with that—use the free licensed instrumental option, keeping the entire clip unchanged and the music clearly below every radio call.

dialog.agent:
**No credits have been spent.** I need to correct my earlier offer: the connected tools can’t fetch a licensed music track or mix it into your clip. I can’t deliver that finished edit here without another tool.

The **zero-credit route** is to use a free editor:
- Choose a tense instrumental explicitly licensed for your intended use; check any attribution requirement.
- Keep the full **7-second clip**, its original audio, and all footage intact.
- Put the music on a separate track, very low beneath every radio call, with an extra dip around **“Rook, you with me?”**

If you have a licensed track, I can give you an **FFmpeg command that copies the video without re-encoding** and mixes only the audio, with automatic music ducking beneath speech. That would cost **0 Magic Hour credits**.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed
